Subject: Private link intermittents — connectivity blips to svc cluster

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing transient packet drops and TCP stalls to the Redwood private endpoint in our prod VPC yesterday evening (roughly 22:30 UTC). The symptoms: short-lived TCP retransmit bursts, some POSTs timing out, and a handful of healthy pods reporting connection reset errors when talking to the inference endpoint. The problem appears to affect only traffic that traverses Halcyon's dedicated private link to your PoP in us-west-2 — public API traffic is fine.

Attached are a quick traceroute and a pcap captured at our edge router for the 22:30-23:15 UTC window. Can you confirm whether anything changed in your private-edge configuration or if you're seeing dropped packets on your side? We're scheduling an internal maintenance window if a fix requires a configuration change.

Thanks,
Merle
Network Engineer — Halcyon Cloud

Folks — I pulled the packet capture Merle attached and compared it against our edge ingress traces. Two observations up-front:
1) The Halcyon pcap shows frames with double 802.1Q tags (outer VLAN 4091, inner VLAN 20), but our collector is seeing single-tagged frames with VLAN 20 only.
2) When double-tagged packets arrive at our edge (we see a small subset), our SNAT path applies a translation based on the untagged outer-header assumption which then results in the packet egressing with a mismatched outer tag after NAT — downstream devices that expect single-tagged traffic drop the return path or mismatch on ACLs.

Tentative hypothesis: an intermediate provider or customer edge is performing QinQ (double tagging) for transit. One of the switches in the path is rewriting or stripping the outer tag inconsistently (sometimes), so our NAT table and SGs see different 802.1Q context between directions — causing asymmetric forwarding and short-lived blackholes. Also seeing small MTU fragmentation spikes consistent with extra tag bytes on some frames.

Action items I recommend immediately:
- Ask Halcyon to check their edge switch trunk config (dot1q tunneling/QinQ) and confirm whether outer VLAN 4091 should be preserved or collapsed. (Merle — can you share the edge-switch-config-snippet.txt?)
- We'll remove tag-dependent logic from the SNAT path temporarily and apply a conservative egress-mangle rule to ensure the outer tag is consistent for return traffic. This will be tested in canary for 30 minutes behind a health check.
- Capture a short, synchronized PCAP from both sides (Halcyon edge + our ingress) for the next incident spike. Align clocks (NTP).

I'm standing by to run the canary when Halcyon is ready.

—Karthik
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

We've attached the requested config snippet and added an inline capture that shows double tags exiting our router. We did a quick check and saw that a provider aggregation switch was recently patched in the last week; we will open an ops ticket with them to validate any change.

We'll stand by for your canary change. If you want us to temporarily collapse the outer tag at our edge for a test, we can coordinate a 15-minute window this afternoon (1800 UTC) but that will affect other tenants.

—Merle

1) Deploy conservative egress rewrite so return packets carry VLAN 4091 consistently.
2) Run automated health checks against your failing flows and monitor RTO and retransmit counters.
3) If metrics improve, we'll keep the change and schedule a deeper config remediation with our infra and the transit provider.

Marissa — please prepare a short customer-facing note confirming the planned 30-minute canary and the expected risk (brief packet reordering during the switch). Evelyn — add NETOPS-8421 to our postmortem queue and capture the relevant dash panels.

Merle — are you good to proceed at 18:00 UTC? If Halcyon prefers collapsing the outer tag on your side instead, state it and we will standby.

—Vanessa

From: Merle Tong <merle.tong@halcyon.com>

Subject: Re: Private link intermittents — connectivity blips to svc cluster

Update: we did a limited trunk collapse at our edge during the 18:00 UTC window on Sep 1 as a test (coordinated with your canary). Post-change metrics: retransmits dropped ~92% in the 30-minute observation window; no service-impacting errors reported by app owners. The provider confirmed a firmware regression on their aggregation switch that caused outer-tag inconsistency under load; they're scheduling a patch for the 10th.

Root cause summary for the runbook: inconsistent QinQ handling in provider aggregation (outer tag 4091 occasionally stripped/rewritten), causing asymmetric VLAN context for our SNAT and SG evaluation which resulted in short-lived blackholes and MTU fragmentation (double tags exceeded path MTU in some frames). Temporary mitigation by ensuring consistent outer-tag on egress (either side) resolves the symptom.

Thanks to Karthik and the team for the swift mitigation. Please keep NETOPS-8421 open until provider patch lands; we'll coordinate a permanent fix (either stable QinQ pass-through or agreed collapse policy).

—Merle
Network Engineer — Halcyon Cloud
